title: How to Choose an Electric Toothbrush: Oscillating vs Sonic
h1: How to Choose an Electric Toothbrush
metaDescription: Oscillating or sonic, which features matter and what to ignore: a simple guide to choosing an electric toothbrush.
lede: Electric toothbrushes range from simple to very expensive. The features that help most are found on inexpensive models too.

p: Oscillating-rotating brushes, mainly from Oral-B, use a small round head that spins back and forth. Sonic brushes, such as Sonicare, use a traditional-shaped head that vibrates very quickly from side to side.
Both types clean well when used properly. Choose based on feel, noise and the cost of replacement heads.
These help most people brush better:
list: A two-minute timer, ideally with 30-second prompts to move to the next area
A pressure sensor, which warns you if you're pressing too hard

p: App tracking, many brushing modes and colored handles are nice to have but don't make a big difference for most people.
You'll replace the head about every three months. Over a few years, head prices can matter more than the price of the handle.

faqs.q: Can I use an electric toothbrush with braces or sensitive teeth?
faqs.a: Many people do, and some brushes offer sensitive modes or special heads. Ask your dentist or orthodontist for a recommendation.

faqs.q: Can family members share a handle?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as each person uses their own brush head. Many brands sell colored rings to tell heads apart.
